useCase.label: Use Case
useCase.what: Shows who uses the system (the actors) and what each of them can do.
useCase.when: At the start of analysis, to agree on the system boundary and functional requirements with the client.
useCase.symbols: Circle: actor · Oval: use case · Frame: system boundary · Line: the actor performs the use case.

class.label: Class
class.what: Shows the structure of the system: classes, their attributes and operations, and the relationships between them.
class.symbols: + before a member: public · 1 and *: multiplicity (one / many) · Arrow: direction of the association.

object.label: Object
object.what: A snapshot of the running system: actual instances of the classes with real values and the links between them.
object.when: To test and explain the class diagram with a realistic example.
object.symbols: Rectangle: object as "name : Class" · Attributes with values · Line: link between two objects.

sequence.label: Sequence
sequence.what: Shows the messages exchanged between the actor, the system and the data, in time order, for one scenario.
sequence.when: To explain an important scenario step by step.
sequence.symbols: Solid line: request · Dashed line: reply · opt: a step that happens under a condition.

collaboration.label: Collaboration
collaboration.what: Shows the same scenario as the sequence diagram, focusing on who talks to whom rather than on time.
collaboration.when: To understand the links between the objects taking part in a process.
collaboration.symbols: Node: object (:name) or actor · Arrow: message · Number: message order.

activity.label: Activity
activity.what: Shows the sequence of steps and decisions in a process from start to finish.
activity.when: To understand a workflow and its branches before programming it.
activity.symbols: Rounded shape: start/end · Rectangle: step · Diamond: decision with two branches.

state.label: State
state.what: Shows the states an entity goes through during its life, and the events that move it from one state to another.
state.when: For entities with a clear lifecycle, such as an order, a loan or a reservation.
state.symbols: Black dot: start · Rounded rectangle: state · Arrow: transition named by its event · Double circle: end.

er.label: Entity-Relationship
er.what: Shows the stored entities, their attributes and the relationships between them; it is the basis of the database.
er.symbols: PK: primary key · FK: foreign key · || : exactly one · o{ : zero or more.

package.label: Package
package.what: Groups classes into logical packages and shows how packages depend on each other.
package.when: To organise a large system and split the work within the team.
package.symbols: Frame: package · Rectangle inside: class · Dashed arrow: dependency.

component.label: Component
component.what: Shows the software parts that make up the system (user interfaces, services, database) and how they depend on each other.
component.when: When designing the system architecture and splitting it into modules.
component.symbols: Double rectangle: user interface · Rectangle: service · Cylinder: database · Hexagon: external service.

deployment.label: Deployment
deployment.what: Shows the devices and servers the system runs on, which components run on each, and how they connect.
deployment.when: When planning how to run and deploy the system.
deployment.symbols: Frame: node (device or server) with its kind in «» · Inside: components · Line: connection and its protocol.
